schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN SALES S ON P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID GROUP BY 1 HAVING (SUM(CASE WHEN S.SALE_DATE BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)) = 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN SALES S ON P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID GROUP BY 1 HAVING (SUM(CASE WHEN S.SALE_DATE BETWEEN '2019-01-01' AND '2019-03-31' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)) = 1
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 selects products whose all sales occurred in the date range '2019-01-01' to '2019-03-31'. Q2 computes a ratio of qualifying sales to total sales and checks if it equals 1, which means all sales are within the range. However, Q2 will return a product even if it has no sales outside the range, but also has no sales at all (division by zero or NULL may occur). The counterexample shows a product with no sales at all, which Q1 excludes and Q2 may include.
counterexample_dsp: A product with no sales at all. Q1 excludes it since there are no rows in SALES to match, while Q2 may return it if division by zero or NULL behavior differs.
